**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**Exit codes are stated for 6 of these 8 commands, and that is the register's coverage rather than an omission here.** A row carries the exit codes measured on _v2_; whether v3 reproduces them is a separate field. Where the register says v3 corrects v2 without recording what it corrects it to, this page says so instead of reprinting the behaviour the rewrite exists to remove.

## `intent claude`

Claude Code integration

```
intent claude <subcommand>
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument     | Type         | Required | Values                                                                    | Notes |
| ------------ | ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `subcommand` | `subcommand` | yes      | `subagents`, `skills`, `rules`, `hook`, `upgrade`, `prime`, `ws`, `start` |       |

**Exit codes.** v3 reproduces the behaviour measured on v2 for this verb.

| Code | When                                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | bare / `--help` / unknown flag / outside a project -- all FOUR produce the identical 189B `error: Unknown claude subcommand. Try: ...` |

## `intent claude subagents`

Manage Claude Code subagents

```
intent claude subagents <verb> [<name>...] [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | idempotent |
| Over MCP        | no         |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type         | Required | Values                                         | Notes |
| -------- | ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `verb`   | `subcommand` | yes      | `list`, `install`, `sync`, `uninstall`, `show` |       |
| `name`   | `string`     | no       |                                                |       |

**Flags**

| Flag            | Takes | Default | What it does                                                           |
| --------------- | ----- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-v`            | no    |         | Show full descriptions in `list`                                       |
| `--force`, `-f` | no    |         | Overwrite an agent manifest that already exists                        |
| `--all`         | no    |         | Every unit this install carries (install) or has installed (uninstall) |

**The register records that v3 corrects v2 on this verb and does not record what it corrects it TO.** The measured exit codes it carries are v2's, and v2's are what the correction exists to change, so they are not reproduced here. `intent claude subagents --help`, and your own binary, are the authority.

## `intent claude skills`

Manage Claude Code skills

```
intent claude skills <verb> [<name>...] [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | idempotent |
| Over MCP        | no         |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type         | Required | Values                                         | Notes |
| -------- | ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `verb`   | `subcommand` | yes      | `list`, `install`, `sync`, `uninstall`, `show` |       |
| `name`   | `string`     | no       |                                                |       |

**Flags**

| Flag            | Takes | Default | What it does                                                                           |
| --------------- | ----- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-v`            | no    |         | Show full descriptions in `list`                                                       |
| `--force`, `-f` | no    |         | Overwrite a skill that was changed here, and report the checksum of what was discarded |
| `--dry-run`     | no    |         | Show what would change, no writes                                                      |
| `--all`         | no    |         | Every unit this install carries (install) or has installed (uninstall)                 |

**v3 corrects v2 here.** v3's `sync` detects a change anywhere in a skill's installed content rather than in SKILL.md alone. **THE MECHANISM IS cc's BUILD DECISION AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT SPECIFIED HERE** -- this row records that the defect is corrected, not how. A parity row that dictates an implementation is asserting a second design authority.

## `intent claude upgrade`

Apply Claude canon to the project

```
intent claude upgrade [flags]
```

|                 |         |
| --------------- | ------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes     |
| Reads or writes | mutate  |
| Undo            | one-way |
| Over MCP        | no      |

**Flags**

| Flag              | Takes | Default | What it does                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ----- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--apply`         | no    |         | Write the canon; without it the command reports only                                     |
| `--force`         | no    |         | Overwrite user-edited canon files (CLAUDE.md without the marker, and .intent_critic.yml) |
| `--skip-settings` | no    |         | Leave .claude/settings.json alone, so no Claude Code session hooks are wired             |

**Exit codes.** v3 reproduces the behaviour measured on v2 for this verb.

| Code | When                 |
| ---- | -------------------- |
| 0    | applied or reported  |
| 1    | canon source missing |

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses. Where a command's exit codes appear above, those _are_ its refusal contract; where they do not, the register has nothing to publish.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
